topic.title: Colgan Air near Buffalo, February 2009: the stall warning shook the control column, the captain pulled back instead of pushing, and the airliner rolled over in under half a minute

shape.name: The wrong reflex
shape.beats: hook: the warning going off in the vehicle, named, with its figure on the instrument -> what the warning means (the part near its limit, in 3D) -> the one trained answer on a flat diagram -> what the person did instead, on the controls -> silence, the part goes over its limit, sub-boom -> what followed, in seconds -> the payoff (the toll, plainly) -> the question the long video answers, looping to the first frame
shape.why: the moment of failure here is a human reflex, not a broken part: setting the trained answer against the hands doing the opposite gives the viewer the tension, and why a trained pilot did it waits for the long video

title: Colgan Air: What Happened After the Stall Warning?
description:
Colgan Air's control column shook near Buffalo. What did the captain do next?
We rebuild the last half minute of the flight in 3D from the NTSB's final report: the stick shaker, the trained answer, the pull the other way, and the roll that followed.
The full minute-by-minute story is on the channel.
Sources: NTSB (Feb 2010).
Based on official investigation reports and published sources. 3D scenes are reconstructions, not actual footage.
